title: Recent questions replay answers from other roles and organizations the same account held
evidence: recentQueries(): `AiOutput::where('requested_by', $user->school_id)->where('feature_type', 'ASK_AI_ASSISTANT')->orderByDesc('id')->limit(5)` — no filter on organization_id or structured_input->role, although ask() stores both (`'organization_id' => $user->organization_id`, `'structured_input' => [... 'role' => $user->role]`, lines 94-108). User::getRoleAttribute/getOrganizationIdAttribute come from the active account profile (User.php:123-156), so one school_id spans several role/org profiles. The cleanup migration only deletes rows already stored as STUDENT (`->where('structured_input->role', 'STUDENT')`), and its own docblock says 'that role decided what the answer was allowed to show'.
impact: Take a person who asked as SBO_OFFICER or ADMIN (answers include the officer directory with school IDs and emails, task assignees, budgets, compliance remarks) and is now signed into a STUDENT profile, or into another organization's profile. The Recent questions list on /dashboard/ask-ai shows those answers word for word. This is a student-sees-others'-IDs leak and a cross-tenant leak that the migration does not cover.
suggested_fix: In recentQueries add `->where('organization_id', $user->organization_id)->where('structured_input->role', $user->role)` (or store and match the active profile id). Add a test where one account asks as SBO_OFFICER in org A, then switches to a STUDENT profile in org B, and recent_queries comes back empty.
verifier_notes: recentQueries (now AskAiService.php:3709) filters only requested_by + feature_type; one school_id can hold several AccountProfiles (AccountProfileController::switch) and ask() stores organization_id and structured_input.role, so answers from another profile are replayed. But the answers were produced for this same person under a profile that was allowed to see them, and while that profile is active they can switch back to it; a real disclosure only arises once the other profile is revoked or deactivated, so 'student sees others' IDs leak' overstates it. The scoping defect itself is real and the migration does not cover it.
corrected_fix: Filter recentQueries by the active profile: ->where('organization_id', $user->organization_id)->where('structured_input->role', $user->role) (both are what ask() stores; for dean office staff $user->role is DEPARTMENT_HEAD on both sides). Add the two-profile test as suggested.

title: Ordinary student questions are routed to staff-only intents and refused with wrong copy
evidence: The missing_submissions keywords include `'missing', 'incomplete', 'lacking'` (lines 224-239) and are checked before clearances (line 265). 'already submitted' routes to submitted_documents (246), 'approve' to pending_approvals (302), 'task'/'assigned' to tasks_workload (273). STUDENT_INTENTS (42-51) has none of these, so answer() returns `'answer' => 'Your account does not have access to this part of the organization, so Ask AI cannot answer that. Ask your organization head to add it to your access.'` (318).
impact: A student asking 'Which clearance signatures am I missing?', 'Why is my clearance incomplete?', 'Has my organization application been approved?' or 'What tasks are assigned to me?' (the dashboard briefing gives students a Tasks pillar) gets a refusal. The refusal tells them to ask their organization head for access, which no head can grant a student.
suggested_fix: Pass the role into the keyword branches. For STUDENT, send 'missing/incomplete' questions that mention clearance/signature/sign to clearances_status (check the clearance keywords before missing_submissions), map 'approved/application' to an allowed student intent or how_to_guide, and send task questions to semantic_rag or a student task answer. Give students a refusal message that does not mention the organization head.
verifier_notes: classifyIntent (AskAiService.php ~322-386): 'missing'/'incomplete' are checked before 'clearance', 'approve' maps to pending_approvals, 'task'/'assigned' to tasks_workload; none of those are in STUDENT_INTENTS, so intentAllowed() fails and answer() returns the 'Ask your organization head to add it to your access' copy. Traced 'Which clearance signatures am I missing?', 'Why is my clearance incomplete?', 'Has my organization application been approved?' and 'What tasks are assigned to me?' to refusals.

title: Substring keyword matching sends questions to the wrong intent
evidence: Str::contains on raw substrings: finance_health matches `'owe'`, `'fee'`, `'paid'` (lines 283-289), so 'allowed', 'however', 'coffee' and 'feedback' hit it. merchandise_orders matches `'order'` (269) before elections (294), so 'In order to vote...' hits it. events_attendance `'event'` (298) is checked before pending_approvals `'approval'` (302). The semantic_rag list contains `'how much is'` (202) and `'search'` (218, which matches 'research').
impact: Examples: 'How many students are allowed to vote?' gets a finance answer (for a student, their own invoices). 'In order to vote what do I need?' gets merchandise orders. 'Which event requests are waiting for approval?' gets the event list, not the approval queue. 'How much is my unpaid fee?' goes to semantic RAG, whose corpus has no finance records for students (`$showFinance = $role !== 'STUDENT' && ...`, line 2976).
suggested_fix: Match whole words with a regex (`/\b(owe|owed|fee|fees|order|orders)\b/`). Check approval phrases ('approval', 'approve', 'waiting for review') before the generic 'event' keyword. Drop 'how much is' from the semantic list, or route it to finance_health when it is followed by balance/fee/owe/budget. Add classifyIntent unit cases for each example.
verifier_notes: Str::contains substring matching: 'How many students are allowed to vote?' skips how-to (how many), hits 'owe' in 'allowed' at finance_health before the election check; 'In order to vote...' hits 'order' -> merchandise_orders; 'Which event requests are waiting for approval?' hits 'event' before the approval check; 'How much is my unpaid fee?' hits 'how much is' -> semantic_rag, and the corpus sets $showFinance = $role !== 'STUDENT' (line 3070). 'search' also matches 'research'.

title: 'Ask again' drops the original topic, so suggested questions come back as a different answer
evidence: `onClick={() => runQuestion(item.question, null)}`. recentQueries returns only id/question/answer/asked_at (AskAiService.php:3622-3627), although the topic is stored in structured_input. With no topic, classifyIntent reroutes the suggested questions: SAO 'What registrations, event files, and approvals are pending?' matches 'event' and becomes events_attendance. Admin follow-up "What compliance requirements, event files, or reports haven't we submitted?" doesn't contain the contiguous phrase "haven't submitted" and becomes events_attendance. 'Which active organizations still need an administrator or were returned?' becomes semantic_rag. DH 'Which organizations in my college are returned or missing an administrator?' becomes missing_submissions.
impact: The same question gives a different answer the second time, and the user sees no reason why. Server and client handle intent inconsistently.
suggested_fix: Return `'topic' => $out->structured_input['topic'] ?? null` (or the stored intent) from recentQueries and pass it in 'Ask again': `runQuestion(item.question, item.topic)`. Add a test that every suggestedQuestions()/follow_ups question classifies to its own topic when the topic is omitted.
verifier_notes: AskAiPage.jsx:495 calls runQuestion(item.question, null); recentQueries returns no topic. Traced the suggested questions without topic: SAO 'What registrations, event files, and approvals are pending?' -> events_attendance; 'Which active organizations still need an administrator or were returned?' -> semantic_rag; DH 'Which organizations in my college are returned or missing an administrator?' -> missing_submissions ('missing' checked before 'missing admin'); Admin "...haven't we submitted?" -> events_attendance. Note the client page is being rewritten by other work, so the fix belongs in whichever page ships.

title: Student balance mixes reserved-order debt into 'invoices' and can say 'all caught up' with money owed
evidence: `$owedTotal = (float) ($balanceRow['total_debt'] ?? 0); $unpaidInvoices = (int) ($balanceRow['unpaid_invoice_count'] ?? 0);`. StudentAccountBalances sets `'total_debt' => round($invoiceDebt + $orderDebt, 2)` and counts only invoices in unpaid_invoice_count. The fee row is gated on `if ($unpaidInvoices > 0)` and says 'You have %d open invoice(s) totaling ₱%s' using $owedTotal. The empty-state answer is 'You are all caught up today! Your account has 0 held clearances, 0 unpaid invoices...' (1014), while the highlight shows `'Account balance' => '₱'.number_format($owedTotal, 2)` in warning tone.
impact: A student whose only debt is an unpaid pending merch order sees 'all caught up' next to a ₱350.00 warning balance and gets no action row. A student with invoices sees an invoice total inflated by order debt, which conflicts with the Statement of Account.
suggested_fix: Use invoice_debt for the invoice row and copy. Add a separate 'Pay or upload proof for reserved orders' row when reserved_order_debt > 0 (link /dashboard/merchandise/my-orders). Gate the 'all caught up' text on total_debt < 0.005, not on the row count.
verifier_notes: Student branch (AskAiService.php ~1025-1110): $owedTotal = total_debt, which StudentAccountBalances computes as invoiceDebt + orderDebt, while the fee row is gated on unpaid_invoice_count and labels the total as invoices. With only reserved-order debt no row is added, so the answer is 'You are all caught up today!' while the Account balance highlight shows a warning amount.

title: Student ballot check ignores voting organizations, other open elections, runoff round and the voting window
evidence: `Election::where('organization_id', $orgId)->where('status', 'active')->get([...])->first(fn ($open) => $open->listsVoter($user->school_id));` then `! ElectionBallot::hasVoted($activeElection->id, $user->school_id, 1)`. DashboardBriefingService::buildStudent uses `$user->votingOrganizationIds()` and filters unvoted elections in the query before taking the first (lines 190, 639-644). Election::openRound() returns 2 during a runoff and null outside the start/end window.
impact: Four cases go wrong. A student on their college profile (which votes in the college's member organizations) is never told to vote. A student who voted in the first active election but not a second is told '0 unvoted active elections'. Runoff voters are never prompted. 'Voting is currently open' shows for an active election outside its window. Ask AI and the home briefing disagree.
suggested_fix: Query `Election::whereIn('organization_id', $user->votingOrganizationIds())->where('status','active')` (plus runoff-phase elections). Keep the elections where `$round = $e->openRound()` is not null, `listsVoter` is true and `! ElectionBallot::hasVoted($e->id, $user->school_id, $round)`. Count them and name the soonest-ending one in the row and the answer.
verifier_notes: Ballot check queries only Election::where('organization_id', $orgId)->where('status','active'), takes the first that listsVoter, then hasVoted(..., 1). It ignores votingOrganizationIds() (college profile), skips other unvoted active elections once the first is voted, never checks round 2 (openRound returns 2 only in the runoff phase, which also need not be status active), and ignores the start/end window that openRound enforces, while the row says 'Voting is currently open'.

title: Archived and pending organizations inflate SAO and Department Head counts and lists
evidence: scopedStudentOrganizationIds for SUPER_ADMIN: `DB::table('organizations')->where('organization_type', 'STUDENT_ORGANIZATION')->pluck('id')`. For DEPARTMENT_HEAD it uses User::scopedOrganizationIds(), which is `Organization::student()->where('college_id', ...)`. Neither filters lifecycle_status. The SAO briefing counts `$incompleteOrgs` from `$this->accreditation->forOrganizations($organizationIds)` (701-702). The DH answer uses `{$organizationIds->count()} student organization(s)` (896, 903). buildMissingSubmissions lists every org in the scope with 'Missing files' (1209-1265).
impact: Archived organizations, which are read only, show as 'Follow up with organizations missing compliance requirements' and in the 'Incomplete orgs' highlight. Pending registrations count as college organizations and are listed as missing files, so the dean and the SAO chase organizations that cannot act.
suggested_fix: Keep scopedOrganizationIds() as the tenant boundary, but intersect it with `lifecycle_status = 'active'` for the compliance and accreditation counts, the DH 'College organizations' figure and buildMissingSubmissions. Pending, returned and archived orgs then appear only in their own queues.
verifier_notes: scopedStudentOrganizationIds (line 2482) for SAO plucks every STUDENT_ORGANIZATION and for DH uses scopedOrganizationIds() (Organization::student()->where('college_id')), neither filtering lifecycle_status. AccreditationStatusService::forOrganizations does not filter either, and buildMissingSubmissions fetches lifecycle_status but never uses it, so archived/pending/returned orgs are listed as 'Missing files' and counted in Incomplete orgs and the DH 'College organizations' figure.

title: SAO grievance answer reports at most 12 unresolved grievances
evidence: `$openGrievances = DB::table('grievances')->whereNotIn('status', ['resolved', 'dismissed'])...->limit(self::ROW_LIMIT)->get(...)`, then `'answer' => "There are {$openGrievances->count()} unresolved grievance(s) in the SAO queue, including {$urgentCount} high or critical urgency case(s)."`. Both counts come from the limited collection (ROW_LIMIT = 12). The daily briefing counts urgent grievances without a limit (691-694).
impact: With 30 open grievances the SAO is told there are 12, and the urgent count can disagree with the daily briefing's urgent figure.
suggested_fix: Compute the totals with separate unlimited count queries (`->count()` and the `LOWER(urgency) in ('high','critical')` count). Use the limited query only for the rows, and say 'showing 12 of N' when rows are truncated.
verifier_notes: buildGrievancesStatus applies ->limit(self::ROW_LIMIT) (12) and derives both the unresolved total and the urgent count from that limited collection; the daily briefing counts urgent grievances without a limit, so the two can disagree once more than 12 are open/urgent.

title: Department Head briefing double-lists financial reports, and its answer can contradict its rows
evidence: $pendingApprovals counts `ApprovalRequest::where('required_role', 'DEPARTMENT_HEAD')->where('status','pending')`. FinancialReportController::submit creates an ApprovalRequest with `'entity_type' => 'financial_report', 'required_role' => ...approvalRole('DEPARTMENT_HEAD')` for every report it sets to pending_department_head, and $pendingReports counts those same reports again as a separate row (839-868). Then `$total = $pendingApprovals + $returnedOrgs + $orgsWithoutAdmin;` (excludes $pendingReports). The answer for total 0 is "Your college oversight queue is clear today ... 0 pending Department Head approvals".
impact: Each submitted report appears twice ('N budget, event, or financial report request(s)' and 'Endorse submitted financial reports'). The answer text never mentions reports, so the copy and the rows can disagree.
suggested_fix: Either drop the separate dh-reports row (the approval request already covers it), or exclude entity_type financial_report from $pendingApprovals and add $pendingReports to $total and to the answer sentence. Point the row at /dashboard/department-head/approvals, the route the sidebar uses (UX_FLOW break 9).
verifier_notes: FinancialReportController::submit sets submission_status pending_department_head and creates an ApprovalRequest with entity_type financial_report and required_role DEPARTMENT_HEAD, so each submitted report is counted in both $pendingApprovals (row dh-approvals) and $pendingReports (row dh-reports): the double listing is real. The second claim, that the answer can say 'clear' while a report row shows, needs a pending_department_head report without a pending approval request, which the submit path never produces, so it is effectively unreachable. /dashboard/approvals already redirects a DH to /dashboard/department-head/approvals (App.jsx:204), so the link change is cosmetic.
corrected_fix: Exclude entity_type financial_report from the DH $pendingApprovals count (or drop the separate dh-reports row) so each report is counted once; the link change to /dashboard/department-head/approvals is optional because /dashboard/approvals already redirects there.

title: SAO approvals row links to the Accreditation tab, not the queue that holds those approvals
evidence: `'href' => $this->routeAccess->hrefFor($role, '/dashboard/super-admin/compliance'), 'action_label' => 'Open queue'` for 'Process SAO approval requests (events & financial reports)'. SaoCompliancePage defaults to the accreditation tab and has separate `event-reviews` and `financial` tabs. The compliance row in the same briefing already uses `?tab=review` (737).
impact: 'Open queue' lands on Organization accreditation, against UX_FLOW rule 6 ('lands on the exact item, not on a list that contains it'). The SAO has to hunt for the event and report reviews.
suggested_fix: Split the count by entity_type and link event approvals to `/dashboard/super-admin/compliance?tab=event-reviews` and financial reports to `?tab=financial` (hrefFor already validates the query).
verifier_notes: The prio-approvals row links to /dashboard/super-admin/compliance with no tab; SaoCompliancePage DEFAULT_TAB is 'accreditation', while event approvals live on the 'event-reviews' tab and financial reports on 'financial' (App.jsx also redirects super-admin/approvals to ?tab=financial).

title: GET /ai/assistant builds and scores the whole RAG corpus on every page load just for metadata
evidence: overview() calls `$this->answer($user, ..., 'daily_priorities', false)`. answer() always runs `$rag = $this->retrieveRagContext($user, $question, $organizationIds, $intent);`, which runs buildKnowledgeCorpus (about 10 queries plus accreditation over every scoped org) and BM25/vector/trigram scoring per document. With allowModel false, $rag is used only for `rag_metadata`. Daily priorities then run their own queries, including a second accreditation pass for the SAO (701).
impact: Every visit to Ask AI pays for a full corpus build and score that changes nothing on the briefing. This costs the most for the SAO and the Department Head, whose corpus spans every organization.
suggested_fix: Skip retrieveRagContext when `$allowModel === false && $intent !== 'semantic_rag'` and return minimal rag_metadata (or null) for the overview briefing.
verifier_notes: answer() always calls retrieveRagContext (line ~409) before branching; overview() calls answer(..., 'daily_priorities', false), where $rag is used only for rag_chunks/rag_metadata since augmentWithRagMatches and the model call are skipped when allowModel is false. Every GET /ai/assistant therefore pays for the full corpus build and scoring.

title: Officer daily briefing shows task counts regardless of the officer's module limits
evidence: `$overdueTasksQuery = DB::table('tasks')->where('organization_id', $orgId)->where('status', 'overdue'); ... if ($isOfficer) { ...->where('assigned_to', $user->school_id); }`, with no `moduleAllowed($user, 'tasks')` check. Merchandise, compliance and events in the same block are gated (1059-1077). tasks_workload is gated via INTENT_MODULES and the corpus via `$this->moduleAllowed($user, 'tasks')` (3219).
impact: An officer limited to, say, finance sees 'Complete your overdue assigned tasks' with a count, but asking 'Who has overdue tasks?' is refused. The briefing and the intent gate disagree.
suggested_fix: Wrap the task counts and rows in `$this->moduleAllowed($user, 'tasks')`, as the other queues are. Alternatively, if officers should always see their own tasks, exempt self-assigned tasks in tasks_workload as well, so the two agree.
verifier_notes: The officer task counts are filtered to assigned_to = the officer, and EnsureOrganizationModule deliberately keeps 'see their own tasks' open (GET api/tasks and PATCH api/tasks/{id}/status are participation routes), so showing an officer's own overdue tasks without a tasks-module check is correct by design. The real defect is the inverse inconsistency: tasks_workload is gated on the tasks module, so 'What tasks are assigned to me?' is refused for that same officer. Wrapping the briefing counts in moduleAllowed (the primary suggested fix) would hide tasks the officer is meant to see.
corrected_fix: Keep the briefing as is. Let tasks_workload answer an SBO_OFFICER whose profile lacks the tasks module with only their own assigned tasks (assigned_to = school_id), instead of refusing, so the briefing and the intent agree.

title: No tests cover profile-scoped history, keyword misroutes or student briefing money and ballot paths
evidence: The only history test stores rows per distinct user (`storeAskAiRow($seeded['student'], 'STUDENT', ...)`, `storeAskAiRow($seeded['officer'], 'SBO_OFFICER', ...)`) and never switches one account between profiles. No test calls classifyIntent with the suggested questions minus their topic, or with words like 'allowed', 'in order to' or 'missing clearance'. No test checks the student briefing's reserved-order debt, runoff or college-profile elections, or the DH briefing with a pending financial report.
impact: askai-core-01 through askai-core-09 can regress, or stay unfixed, without any test failing.
verifier_notes: AskAiAssistantTest's only history test stores rows for distinct users and never switches one account between profiles; no test exercises classifyIntent with topic-less suggested questions or the misroute words, the reserved-order-only balance, runoff/college-profile elections, or a DH with a submitted financial report. Coverage gap applies to the findings that stand (01-09, 12-14).
